title: Jim Sarbh Is Xerxes Desai and Naseeruddin Shah Is JRD Tata in Made in India: A Titan Story. It Drops June 3.
excerpt: The series about how a Tata Group subsidiary turned a ₹50 watch into India's most trusted consumer brand arrives on Amazon MX Player this week.
body:
Before Titan was the brand that sold a billion watches, it was a boardroom argument inside the Tata Group about whether India could manufacture its own quartz timepiece. That argument — and the man who won it — is now a streaming series.

*Made in India: A Titan Story* premieres on Amazon MX Player on June 3. Jim Sarbh plays Xerxes Desai, the visionary businessman who turned Titan from an improbable idea into India's most successful consumer brand. Naseeruddin Shah is JRD Tata, the patriarch whose backing made the whole thing possible.

## The Real Story Behind the Show

The series is adapted from Vinay Kamath's book *Titan — India's Most Successful Consumer Brand*, which traces the company's journey from a joint venture between the Tata Group and the Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO) in 1984 to the ₹2.5 lakh crore market cap behemoth it is today.

Xerxes Desai's story is remarkable. He took a country that imported 90% of its watches and convinced it to manufacture its own — and then to prefer its own. By the time Titan's Tanishq jewellery line and Fastrack youth brand became household names, Desai had fundamentally changed how India thought about consumer brands.

Director Robby Grewal brings the story to screen with a cast that includes Vaibhav Tatwawadi, Namita Dubey, Lakshvir Saran, and Kaveri Seth. During promotions in Mumbai, Namita Dubey shared that she was "slightly intimidated" by Jim Sarbh's intense acting process — his spatial awareness and spontaneous line changes kept the entire set on their toes — but found comfort in Grewal's encouraging direction.

## Why This Matters for the Diaspora

Every Indian household abroad owns at least one Titan product. The brand is as embedded in NRI life as Parle-G biscuits and Amul butter. For many first-generation immigrants, a Titan watch was the last gift they received before boarding a flight — a graduation present from a father, a wedding gift from an in-law, a retirement memento from a colleague.

The show arrives at a moment when "Make in India" has become both a government initiative and a cultural aspiration. Titan's original story predates the slogan by three decades, but the parallels are deliberate. The series explicitly connects to the spirit of building Indian manufacturing capability — turning a country of consumers into a country of creators.

Jim Sarbh, who has quietly become one of Indian cinema's most reliable actors (from *Padmaavat* to *Rocket Boys* to *Made in Heaven*), brings the right combination of intellectual intensity and emotional vulnerability that Desai's story demands. Naseeruddin Shah as JRD Tata is casting that needs no justification.

## What to Expect

The series streams on Amazon MX Player starting June 3. For a diaspora audience that grew up watching its parents check the time on a gold-rimmed Titan Raga or a silver Sonata, this is nostalgia wrapped in a business story wrapped in national pride.

It's also a reminder that the most interesting Indian stories aren't always about politics or Partition or family drama. Sometimes they're about a man who looked at a ₹50 HMT watch and said: we can do better.

*Made in India: A Titan Story streams on Amazon MX Player from June 3, 2026.*
author: Diaspora Desk
